# Telescope (refractor) (`telescope`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/physics.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Physics, optics & astronomy (`physics`)
- Deps: needs lenses; helped by clear_glass, refraction_optics
- Core idea: A weak convex lens of long focal length at the front (objective) and a strong lens of short focal length at the eye, held in a tube that can slide to focus. With a concave eyepiece (Dutch or Galilean form) the image is upright and the tube length is the difference of the two focal lengths; with a convex eyepiece (Kepler's form) it is inverted, the field is wider and the length is the sum. The magnification is the objective's focal length divided by the eyepiece's: a spectacle lens focusing at 1 m with an eyepiece of 5 cm gives 20 times. Covering the outer part of the objective with a ring of card sharpens the image. Twenty times shows Jupiter's four moons, the mountains of the Moon, the phases of Venus and ships hours before the naked eye.
- Pitfalls:
  - Two lenses of similar strength give no magnification
  - Ordinary spectacle glass is too poor at more than a few times; Galileo ground his own and rejected most lenses
  - Colour fringes and blur grow with lens diameter; not stopping down the objective
  - Looking at the Sun through it (blinds); project the image on paper instead
  - Crediting Galileo with the invention
- History: europe: 1608 – Lipperhey applies for a patent in The Hague (Metius and Janssen also claim it); 1609 Harriot and Galileo turn it to the sky; 1611 Kepler describes the two-convex-lens form; china: 1626 – Schall von Bell's treatise on the telescope; india: c. 1616 – a telescope among Thomas Roe's gifts at Jahangir's court; 1618 Jesuits observe comets by telescope from Goa; east_asia: 1613 – a telescope presented to Tokugawa Ieyasu by the English East India Company
- Read:
  - Galileo Galilei, Sidereus Nuncius (1610)
  - Albert Van Helden, The Invention of the Telescope (1977)
